**22 palavras novas** (pensamento crítico).
**Texto do dia:** texto acadêmico e resumo.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever sobre argumentação a partir de um texto acadêmico e usar weigh in on.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

frames.title: Reading · An academic text with abstract

blocks.title: Abstract: Causation and Correlation
paras: This paper examines why correlation is often mistaken for causation. Using three case studies, we show that a **third variable** can create a spurious link between unrelated events. We argue that readers should **weigh in on** causal claims only after considering **alternative explanations**.
Findings suggest that **randomised trials** reduce, though cannot eliminate, such errors.

items.q: A third variable can create a false link.

blocks.body: O *abstract* tem 4 movimentos: **objetivo, método, tese, resultado**. Verbos de relato no presente; hedging nos resultados (*suggest, indicate*).

items.s: We ___ that readers should check alternatives. (argue)
Experts will ___ in on the claim. (weigh)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Correlation is not causation.** — Correlação não é causalidade.
**Rule out.** — Descartar.
**Beyond a reasonable doubt.** — Além de dúvida razoável.
**Burden of proof.** — Ônus da prova.
**Cause and effect.** — Causa e efeito.
**A confounding factor.** — Fator de confusão.
**By chance.** — Por acaso.
**Draw conclusions.** — Tirar conclusões.
**Test a hypothesis.** — Testar uma hipótese.
**What does the paper argue?** — O que o artigo defende?
**Do randomised trials solve it?** — Ensaios aleatorizados resolvem?
**They reduce errors but cannot eliminate them.** — Reduzem erros, mas não os eliminam.

lines: That readers should weigh alternative explanations before judging a causal claim.

items.label: Pausas e ritmo
items.note: Pausas e ritmo: faça uma pausa curta entre grupos de sentido e acelere as palavras fracas entre os acentos.
words: The claim, | although popular, | lacks support.
If the sample is small, | the result is weak.
To be fair, | the study | has limits.

prompts.q: Summarise the abstract in one sentence.
prompts.model: The paper argues that correlation is often mistaken for causation.
A third variable, such as wealth, could explain it.

prompts.q: Weigh in on a claim politely.
prompts.model: If I may weigh in on that, I’d like more evidence.

blocks.task: Write a 5-sentence abstract about a small study you could imagine.
blocks.model: This study examines whether sleep affects exam scores. Using a survey of 200 students, we show that sleep and scores are positively linked. We argue that this link may reflect a third variable, such as stress. Findings suggest that sleep matters, though causation cannot be proven. Further research should use randomised trials.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
